text_fidelity_a:
Withings Go | Activity & Sleep tracker I spent hours trying to get this Nokia Health Mate Go ("Nokia") to work.

Bottom line: This is a worthless piece of junk.

Here is what I did:

1. I installed the Nokia on my iPhone 5c with associated app. The app indicated that it recognized the Nokia.
2. I put it on my left wrist and walked all over my house to test its pedometer's accuracy in counting steps. After ten minutes, it still registered zero steps. Clearly it did not record or update steps properly.
3. I tried to figure out why the device, in this regard, was not communicating well with the iPhone app. I finally employed the computer programmer's tried-and-true cure-all: I did the nearest to a "reboot" that I could. I killed the app and then restarted it.
4. I started walking again, and it was at least trying to record the steps. But all it did was state, "Looking for your tracker...."
5. Finally the app updated, and then it started to finally count steps. I then killed the app and started it again to refresh it.
6. I did a test. I walked while counting my steps myself, speaking them out loud. After 165 steps, I looked down at the Nokia. It said I had taken 55 steps.

This thing is a bust as a pedometer, and I couldn't figure out anything else it is useful for. Of all things, it can't even measure the heart rate.

This is NOT a cheaper alternative to a Fitbit. It is not good for anything. If you want a pedometer, I suggest buying one.
text_fidelity_b: Withings Go | Activity & Sleep tracker

text_fidelity_a:
Reliance Products Aqua-Tainer 7 Gallon Rigid Water Container (Pack of 2) I've owned this brand and style of water container for almost 17 years, it's my go-to for camping and day trips where there might not be any water. I have almost always had at least 2 of them, one for drinking water, the other for potable water (cleaning dishes, cooking, dog water). Recently having to purchase two more, I guess the one that's put on the age and seen places finally developed a crack on the bottom. Not bad after 7-8 years being lugged around.

Pros: Lots of water on hand - Easy to use - Stack able - Durable - Trusted brand -

Cons: Heavy once full (7gallons x 7lbs per gallon of water + container = 50lbs) - spigot almost never lines up pointing down no matter how many ways you screw on the cap - price raised by $10 in past year

Points to look at when choosing: If you can't lift 7 gallons, get the 2.5 or 5 gallon model
(Here is an example per the National Park Service) 2 gallons a day per person when camping, you can figure the same if the water at your house is shut off during a emergency event. You might add an extra gallon for toilet flushes.
text_fidelity_b: Reliance Products Aqua-Tainer 7 Gallon Rigid Water Container (Pack of 2)

text_fidelity_a:
Clement Cycling Strada LGG Clincher 120 TPI Tire I recently bought a new Specialized Sirrus hybrid bicycle. Toady I swapped out the OEM tires and tubes for Clement Cycling Strada LGG 120 TPI 700cx28 clincher tires and Continental MTB/Race 28 700x25-32 tubes with 60mm Presta valves. The LGG tires weigh 233g each (my actual measurements), compared to 478g for the stock Espoir Sport Reflect 700x30c tires. The width of the LGG's on the stock 26mm (outside width) rims is 29.8mm, compared to 32.4mm for the stock tires. The Conti tubes weigh 140g, compared to 154g for the stock tubes. The overall weight savings was a surprising 259g, or 9.14oz, for each wheel.

Riding at the same tire pressure, 70 lbs front and 75 lbs back, the LGG tires had much quicker handling and the ride felt more cushioned. The more cushioned ride may be due to the heavy, relatively stiff carcass on the stock tires compared to the very lightweight and flexible sidewalls on the LGGs.
text_fidelity_b: Clement Cycling Strada LGG Clincher 120 TPI Tire

text_fidelity_a:
MARK LAUREN Bodyweight Workout DVD Mobility Rx DVD Set I have owned this 2-DVD set for several weeks now, and I am still on the fence about it. I researched it thoroughly before I purchased it, and the overall reviews seemed very positive. I am a daily exerciser and also a yoga instructor, but as I get older (I'm 49 now), I definitely have increasing aches and pains, and I know there are times when my lack of flexibility limits my yoga practice. I was hoping that Mark Lauren's Mobility Rx set would benefit me in these areas.

I will first provide a brief overview of the workouts, then detail what I liked/didn't like. Both DVDs have a Main Menu which includes selection for Introduction (Lauren's 2-minute explanation of these workouts, which you can find on YouTube), Warm Up (the same for both workouts, and Workout (1 or 2). There is also an option for Music on/off and Closed Captioning on/off.

The Warm-up is what Lauren calls a "movement prep," and it clocks in at 9:39 minutes. In has nice, full-body joint mobility work such as windshield wiper knees, hydrant hip rotations, trunk rotations, one leg bridges, lunges with torso twist, squat, and lunges with lateral reach. Workout #1 is 34 minutes total, including a 4 1/2 minute description of each of the four exercises. (Note that it is NOT easy to skip this. You can select the workout from the Main Menu without doing the Warm-up, but it is also NOT easy to return to the Main Menu AFTER doing the Warm-up for some reason.) There are three rounds in this workout, and they clock in at 8:53, 9:22, and 11:12. The exercises are side-lying snow angel, isometric lunge, zombie squat, and scorpion complex, and they get progressively more challenging with each round. Workout #2 has the same structure but with different exercises. This workout is shorter, with 3 1/2 minute introduction and three rounds of 7:24, 7:37, and 8:14 to clock at 27 minutes total. The exercises are seated roll, straddle reach, spider crawl, and gate swing complex. All of the exercises are well-described in other reviews for those wanting more details.

What I like about Mobility Rx is much shorter than what I don't like, so I will start with that.

WHAT I LIKED ABOUT THESE WORKOUTS:
*The exercises themselves. For the most part, these felt like functional fitness movements that definitely have the potential to benefit my body.
*The Warm-up. Although almost 10 minutes is long for a warm-up, this would make a nice little stand-alone stretch routine; it could also work as a cool-down after other activity.

Okay, that's about all I can think of, so on to what I didn't like.

WHAT I DIDN'T LIKE ABOUT THESE WORKOUTS:
*The fact that they are on 2 separate DVDs. This may seem minor, but there's only a little over an hour of content, so making this set 2 separate DVDs not only feels wasteful to me but also feels like a marketing gimmick, as if they are trying to deceive customers.
*The very poor production values. Honestly, I often don't even notice these types of things on workout DVDs (and I have literally tried 100s), but there were MULTIPLE issues here, including the following: 1) the music - it was just bad, loud and on a repetitive loop (although at least there was a music off option), 2) the sound - it was out of sync with the screen, which is VERY annoying if you are actually looking at Lauren while doing the workout, 3) the menus - as mentioned above, options such as skipping forward and returning to the Main Menu did not work correctly, and 4) the set - also just awful, with a frame around the screen that appears as if you are looking into a 1980s computer and empty fake wood boxes stacked in the corner for no reason
*Lauren's instruction. Other than telling viewers to stand or sit with "tall PRETTY posture"--an awful expression that he uses over and over--he provides little instruction on form and absolutely no modifications. The initial preview of the exercises for each workout offers an anatomical view of the muscles being worked, but Lauren never refers back to this during the workouts themselves, never connecting the movements with the actual benefits for the body.
*The disparity between the two workouts. As you can see by my description above, the first workout is significant longer than the second, but it is also MUCH harder. The second exercise, the isometric lunge, is actually a lunge with the shin placed vertical against a wall/other structure. I would consider this an advanced movement--I have done it in yoga classes only after significantly more prep work than Lauren provides here. Similarly, the fourth exercise, scorpion complex, also incorporate yoga-type movements (plank and downward facing dog), and it requires a good deal of stamina and endurance.

In summary, I believe that these routines are appropriate ONLY FOR EXPERIENCED EXERCISERS. Although I definitely fall into that category myself, and I do see some utility to the movements Lauren offers here, the downsides of this set are a significant detraction for me, and I have not yet decided whether or not I will keep it.
text_fidelity_b: MARK LAUREN Bodyweight Workout DVD Mobility Rx DVD Set

Sleepingo Sleeping Pad for Camping - Ultralight Sleeping Mat for Camping, Backpacking, Hiking - Lightweight, Inflatable & Compact Camping Air Mattress (Blue) This is good example of why you can't rely on high reviews on Amazon alone. I consider myself a pretty durable sleeper; not overly picky or sensitive to sleep conditions. That said, this sleeping pad is next to worthless, especially if you are planning to camp on uneven/rocky ground. Its primary faults are that it is far too thin (about 1.5 inches when inflated), it is too small, and it slips around way too easily in the tent. With regards to thickness, if you sleep on your side, or if there are any rocks/pebbles under you, you will feel them digging into your hips. Compounding this problem is the fact that the pad is too small and too slippery, which makes keeping it positioned under the sleeping bag difficult throughout the night. It is CONSTANTLY shifting around.

Needless to say, it was definitely not worth the money for me. Do your research and don't just purchase the first well reviewed camping pad you run across on Amazon. A lot of them on here are designed similarly to this one. The good air pads are usually 3+ inches thick and quite a bit more expensive. Or, if you are just planning to camp a short distance from the car, go for a tried and true foam pad. They will be much more stable and provide more reliable padding.
text_fidelity_b: Sleepingo Sleeping Pad for Camping - Ultralight Sleeping Mat for Camping, Backpacking, Hiking - Lightweight, Inflatable & Compact Camping Air Mattress (Blue)

text_fidelity_a:
Michelin A1 Aircomp Ultralight Fahrrad Schlauch 28´´ I bought two of these at Performance bike shop because they were on sale. Smooth stems looked nice.
Both of them came apart at the seam. One lasted a few miles from home, another lasted little longer but otherwise more walking distance to home. I had a patch kit and a pump but no use. At least I got refund when took them back to the store. I explained the store clerk what had happened and he wasn't even surprised.
I had different brands of tubes mostly cheap store brand in the past but nothing compare to this. I was very surprised because this happened to well-known name.
What I learned from this. 1) Don't buy anything says ultra light. 2) Don't buy anything only because it's a well-known brand name, it was probably made by another company.
I weigh 140lbs, so the weight wasn't an issue, just in case you are wondering. I inflated it 120psi. Size of the tire was 700x20c.
You can avoid pinch flat snake bites by inflating the tire to certain pressure. If the tire picks up a broken staple, it gets flat but you can patch it. When the tube comes apart, you can't do anything specially if the spare you happen to have has the same defect.

I'll never buy it and I don't recommend this to anybody.
text_fidelity_b: Michelin A1 Aircomp Ultralight Fahrrad Schlauch 28´´

text_fidelity_a: Epiphany Outdoor Gear Pocket Bellows - Weatherproof Collapsible Fire Bellowing Tool for Starting Fire- an Essential Camping Gear After years of blowing at camp fires through pursed lips and getting a face and eyes and lungs full of smoke, I saw a product demonstrated on a Bush Craft video.  It was only available in Europe...  Then I found this on Amazon.  It is stainless steel so it is not light weight for its (small) size.  Its value is in its function and in its collapsiblity.  From a collapsed state of just under 4 inches, it extends to 19 inches,  The larger (.5 inches, diameter) end is placed in the mouth and the narrow end concentrates  oxygenated air from your lungs to a focused stream at the narrow end. Once an initial spark or flame has begun to produce an ember, combustion can be sped up by directing more air precisely at the ember.  That sure beats watching helplessly while the initial spark fails to catch and fades to nothing.  On a dry day with dry, finely processed wood, this might not be needed...but on a cold, damp day with wood that is a bit damp, this makes all the difference between fire and failure.  At first, this device will be stiff to open and close but a little lubricant will help.  Opened up, the rod is sturdy and should last for a good many fires.
text_fidelity_b: Epiphany Outdoor Gear Pocket Bellows - Weatherproof Collapsible Fire Bellowing Tool for Starting Fire- an Essential Camping Gear

text_fidelity_a:
TosGad Yellow Sunglasses for Men, Polarized Reduce Glare and Enhance Vision in Rainy, Foggy UPDATE: We've had rain today so wore these out - have to say, they were great. Please read on for my earlier thoughts regarding them overall and night, but I am adding this - I like them. We are in a state that rainy weather can cause glares and that gray palate that makes elements blend together. We also have a rainy season over 4 months, so it is something that causes me to sometimes wear sunglasses in order to see better. But that makes it even darker. I put these on and it brightened everything. Had my wife try and she too felt there was a brightness. She didn't like them in that she didn't loose the glare per se, however, I did. But for rain, I will most certainly use them - night time, I'm still 50/50.

I had lasik eye surgery a number of years ago and ever since when I drive at nights, lights have “star bursts” and while I can see easily, it’s a bit of a stressor on my eyes - the bright lights can make me squint. So I saw these - and many like them over the months - and I thought I’d give them a try. No idea why, but why not.

1. They fit well and look somewhat cool - though my wife has now refereed to me as George Michael several times. I like them.

2. I don’t know that they work. Or what they are supposed to work for. But, they do something.
I feel it like this: there are those bright white-blue LED lights in many homes now. You can see them stand out brightly - apart from the softer, warmer, yellow or orange lights we grew up with. When I drive/walk/am out at night I can see fine with the white-blue cold lights, but I’ll find myself squinting against them at times, even feeling stress on my eyes from the harshness of them. But with these glasses, they warm and soften these bright white-blue, cold lights and make them more like the softer, warmed, yellow-orange ones. This cuts my squinting and feeling of stress. So Yes, they DO something and DO work, but I’m not even sure if that’s what’s supposed to be happening. It’s what I experience.

3. I still see star bursts on lights, these have not changed that at all. I have not worn in rain yet, but if there is any similarity, they only change the coloring, they do not make anything. sharper, easier to see, or enhanced. But they DO something that makes it a little more comfortable.

I can’t give them a 5 because while they do something I honestly thought they’d do more. I fell like that is the implication. But, I also did feel a bit of stress relief and comfort in these over the sharpness of the LED bright white-blue increasingly on the roads and signage. So I have to give them 4 because I did feel something positive.
text_fidelity_b: TosGad Yellow Sunglasses for Men, Polarized Reduce Glare and Enhance Vision in Rainy, Foggy

Anyway, it seems like they got everything right, but just be advised that this is NOT the type of case where you can see your phone through the top, despite saying it's compatible with all these devices; that's just a way to add search terms, and I guess it's technically correct that those phones will fit in this bag.

While I haven't had this out in a downpour, it has what appear to be excellent quality, self-sealing zippers on the exterior that should be essentially waterproof as far as rain goes (likely not submersible). It's sort of a "shell" case in that it is semi-rigid, and the material has a checkered carbon fiber look to it, which is neat looking and will likely match a lot of fancier bikes, but will work with anything since it's basically black.

The three straps come large enough that I imagine they can be used with any bike, and can be adjusted down as necessary; I expect the cleanest and nicest installations will involve trimming the excess. The one strap is "across" the opening of the two sections, which would limit how far you can open it, except there is a piece of fabric inside artificially limiting how far you can open it, perhaps so that the former's limitation is not so obvious, but I suspect it will help keep you from dropping stuff out of the case while it is installed on the bike.

One side is a half-height net, and the other side is a full height zippered net, both of which offer some stretch, and are very much like a good piece of luggage.

This definitely adds a little bulk to your bike, and I'm not convinced everyone will want on for permanent storage (there are lots of other placement options to consider), but I can imagine that this goes quite far when doing multi-day riding with camping stops. The great thing is that it can be taken off and put back on quite easily, and as needed.
text_fidelity_b: WILD MAN Bike Bag, Bike Accessories, Bike Phone Holder Bike Phone Mount, Waterproof Bike Phone Bag, Mountain Bike Accessories for Adult Bikes with 3D Hard EVA, TPU Touch Screen and Sun Visor for Phones Under 6.7"

Kamagon is approximately the size of a basketball. The easy-grip handles on each side make it bigger. The handles are easy to grab during the exercises. On the back of the Owner's Manual it says, "works the muscles while simultaneously training your nervous system." Yes, I can feel my brain working as my muscles and brain adjust to the movement of the water inside of the ball.

The DVD has two vigorous workouts. The Owner's Manual has workouts with clear black and white photos. There is also plenty of online support via the Kamagon website, facebook, and YouTube. There is a "Kamagon Workout Guide" included. You can eventually work up to five days a week with two days set aside for rest.

Be sure to read and follow the Owner's Manual before starting.

This ball had a strong odor when it first arrived -- I could smell it from across the room. I placed it outside overnight and now I can barely detect any smell at all.

I love this workout method that promotes balance, strength, aerobic endurance and neuromuscular coordination.

The workout works out both core, heart and strength training! 3 in 1!

text_fidelity_a:
Penn International VIS 2 Speed Reel, Gold, 30 What a great reel for big, powerful fish! If you target fish that measure in the hundreds of pounds, and you want the best tool for the job, this is your reel. In my case, it's the reel I use when we go deep for big halibut here in Alaska. This reel holds plenty of line to get to those shelves 400 feet down where the barndoors lie, with plenty of line left over to allow for long runs that those big fish make. If you hang up and break off, losing several hundred feet of line (it happens), you don't have to hang it up because the reel holds enough line to let you keep fishing.

I like the high-speed retrieve for pulling up from the deep when you need to check your bait or try something else. When you latch into a fish, though, a quick push of the button on the hub of the handle engages the more powerful lower gears, so you can really torque into the fish.

That new handle design is nice, too. It comfortably fits my hand, has a nice rubbery, no-slip texture, and helps spread the stress across the meaty part of my hand so long battles are just a little bit easier.

The open design of the "X" series frame (with no crossbars across the front of the spool) is helpful when there's a backlash to deal with (yeah, it still happens once in a while). These reels aren't cheap, but they're the best you can buy. Solid, reliable, and made in USA. No regrets here!

Let me know if you don't anything in my review helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Penn International VIS 2 Speed Reel, Gold, 30

text_fidelity_a:
PLUSINNO Fishing Reel, 5.7:1 High Speed Spinning Reel,9 +1BB,Premium Drag System with17-22 LB Max Drag,Ultra Smooth Powerful, Lightweight Graphite Frame, CNC Aluminum Spool for Saltwater Freshwater i picked up a sougilyang spinner reel for $20, comes w spare spool and overall feels great. felt more like a $40-50 reel. i have a few kastking reels i nabbed for $50 and felt like $80... even one that had issues outta the box cuz incorrect assembly was still awesome after i fixed it.

the plussino reel however did not get that same emotion.

at first glance, its a gorgeous reel. definitely looks like a $80 reel. my buddy’s cheapo $15 reel? definitely looked cheapo with plastic parts falling off. so the plussino has that, along with a smooth retrieve.

its biggest issue was the drag and some really sharp edges... and its heavy!

the drag was a mess. i had to take apart the drag completely and found metal shavings in the felt. there were also some imperfections and cross threading happening here and there. even with it cleaned out, drag was still super rough. wasnt till i added some drag grease that it gotten smoother.

then the sharp edges. the machining on the spool looks “sharp!” haha puns - the slotting in the spool is literally sharp. i had to go across it a few times with some ceramic rods to clean and smooth it out.

its also a pretty heavy reel for its size - wished i paid attention to that. whereas other reels of this size are in the 8-10 oz range, this feels much heavier.

am i happy with it? meh. its what i paid for so i cant complain (but i just did complain! lol) - it’ll suit its purpose as a backup reel. its just, i was hoping for the same fit/finish and waulity reel vs some of their other competitors which ive had good luck eith.

it doeeesss look sexy tho on the plussino rod.
text_fidelity_b: PLUSINNO Fishing Reel, 5.7:1 High Speed Spinning Reel,9 +1BB,Premium Drag System with17-22 LB Max Drag,Ultra Smooth Powerful, Lightweight Graphite Frame, CNC Aluminum Spool for Saltwater Freshwater

text_fidelity_a: Sawyer Products SP105 MINI Water Filtration System, Single, Black We absolutely love this little water filter, we bought it in hopes of replacing an old MSR ceramic core filter (which I still love and will continue to be used on "car-camping" trips) because of the weight savings.  This weighs practically nothing and even including the water pouches and the syringe in case of clogging, takes up very little room.  It filters very fast, my dad is always telling other gear heads that his Katadhin water filter is the fastest out there... and this little filter beat his 2 out of 3 times.  The one thing I would warn prospective buyers of is that it works best if you have a collapsible bucket.  By scooping up our water and then letting the sediment settle before filling the pouches we were able to avoid clogging.  When we just did quick refills on the go (immersing the pouch right from the water source) we experienced more clogging.  Even so, clogs aren't a big deal to take care of, just another quick minute to backflush with the syringe and its good to go.  The other thing I really liked about this one vs. our old school filter is that it is much easier to clean after the trip before it is packed into storage.  You don't have to take anything apart worry about losing small vital parts.
text_fidelity_b: Sawyer Products SP105 MINI Water Filtration System, Single, Black

EnerPlex Queen Air Mattress with Built in Pump - 13" Luxury Size Self-Inflating Blow Up Mattress with Neck Support - Inflatable Air Bed for Portable Travel & Home Use (Blue/White) First let me start this review by saying that IF I purchased this air mattress to use at home, I would be giving it 5 stars. It is super comfy. However, I bought it to go camping as it is advertised as suitable for camping but it only offers an electric plug to power on the inflation pump.
I ended up simply purchasing a $10 converter cigarette lighter to 110v outlet, to plug in so that I can plug the pump in to inflate. While it fills super fast it is awkward to carry from the car back to my tent, but the comfort is worth it.
It does need to be "topped off" with air every night but that is to be expected and is normal air loss. Again however, a bit of a hassle to pull it out of my tent, carry it to the car, fill it up and then take it back to my tent. My puppy dog (ok she's 75 pounds so maybe not a puppy) jumped on it a few times and the material was able to handle her nails with no issues.
So if you are using this for company at your home or are an RV camper with a generator then get this air mattress, you won't be disappointed. If you don't mind a little bit of inconvenience and willing to buy an adapter so that you can fill it while camping, then you too will sleep great!
text_fidelity_b: EnerPlex Queen Air Mattress with Built in Pump - 13" Luxury Size Self-Inflating Blow Up Mattress with Neck Support - Inflatable Air Bed for Portable Travel & Home Use (Blue/White)

Micoop Wide Brim Military Camouflage Hat Summer Fishing Hunting Camping Hiking Cap Outdoor Sun Hat Boonie Hat Working outside in sunny and humid Southwest Florida requires a lot of protection from the sun and bugs -- especially as you get older. I ordered this particular boonie type hat because it offered a wide brim, UV protection (SPF 50), adjustability, and mesh covers over the breathing holes. The mesh covered holes are a nice touch during our 95 degree plus days because they keep the bugs out while still allowing a bit of air to circulate under the hat.

I wore my last boonie hat until it virtually rotted. When I removed this new hat from the packaging I was immediately impressed with the quality of the construction and the vividness of the colors (Military Green). There is no question that this new Micoop Wide Brim Military Camouflage Hat is a big step up in quality from my old boonie. The material is thicker, the grommets for the breathing holes are properly anchored, and the adjustable chin strap makes it easy to get a comfortable fit.

My normal hat size is 7 3/8. While this particular hat runs big, it can be adjusted to fit properly. Combining that with all the other features and you end up with a great hat for the money. As an added bonus, when I tried it on for my kids at the dinner table, they said that they couldn't see me when I had it on. I guess that the camouflage works too!
text_fidelity_b: Micoop Wide Brim Military Camouflage Hat Summer Fishing Hunting Camping Hiking Cap Outdoor Sun Hat Boonie Hat

text_fidelity_a:
Misfit Shine - Activity and Sleep Monitor I am posting a "reserved" review...After the experience buying the black one for my husband and the first one arrived, opened and not working! (BAD Amazon order fufillers sending an obviously opened and non-functioning product) I have had my Shine for about a week... I wear in on my wrist most of the time.. I chose to remove it before bathing. If I were swimming I would leave it on, although the propoganda states that if you wear in "treated" water it reduce it's life - odd to me. Also, it doesn't auto sync. You must sync it to your phone each day. The upside is that you don't have to charge it, just replace the battery. It seems to be fairly accurate. I will update if there are any use/wear issues. It arrived quickly (I have prime) and in good condition.

UPDATE 10/15/2014..... So... I've been using the Shine for about a month... it hasn't failed, to my knowledge. It syncs when prompted to, although I have found sometimes it takes longer than others even though I set it right next to my phone each time. It has survived one system "update" without noticeable issues. I chose to remove it when bathing. I do wish it auto synced rather than to manually prompt it to do so every morning. I have learned that if you are interested in following your sleep pattern one night at a time (it doesn't provide a graph of experience, however you can review night by night - would be nice to have an over all view), you must use the wrist band. Using the magnetic clip does not provide sleep info. Also note: when using the magnetic clip, be aware that it is HIGHLY likely to detach from you and attach to something else magnetic if it gets close and you may not even notice that you've left your Shine on something else. The "watch" band seems to be very durable. The time option of the Shine is interesting and maybe entertaining for a short while, however, it is not as "obvious" as you might think. It is very easy to misread. I found myself double-checking my phone a lot because I would think... hmm... my Shine says 5:30 but I KNOW it's 6:30. I eventually chose to "turn off" the watch function. Which is another thing.. to change anything you must be attached to where ever you downloaded the progam, not an option on the Shine itself. All of this is just information for those of you who are researching options. Honestly, the best part of the Shine for me is the battery and not having to charge it each night or every few nights. I didn't think I would mind the wrist band, but I am bored with it and it's look now, which sometimes interfers with my jewelry options. I considered the necklace accessory, however, the reviews of it were overwhelming not so great, so I stuck with the wrist band and the clip that comes with it. Over all it seems to fairly accurately record movement. However, when this one fails, I am probably going to search out the next option unless they do the subtle upgrades mentioned above... but even then, I think I'm still looking for the device that works best for me. Hope this info helps you in your research!
UPDATE: NOV 18 2014.... Sooo...about 2 months in and now it sometimes doesn't sync the sleep info. Randomly it just fails. And it would be nice if it would provide a graph or chart or some analysis of your sleep and workout info... but nope. It does now sync with My fitness pal, which is a free easy way of keeping track of your food/calories. Honestly, it's still disappointing because there are so many others that offer you more for about the same amount of money.

UPDATE: 12/4/2014.... Ok... the shine has officially stopped syncing... it's been "sputtering"... not recording data... taking a really long time to sync... etc.. I tried replacing the battery just in case. So... in less than 3 months.. it has stopped working. I would NOT recommend this pedometer at all. You would like to think it work for at least a year! I have the first gen fit bit... I just wanted one I could wear on my wrist. Honestly, I think I will try the wrist model of the fitbit.
text_fidelity_b: Misfit Shine - Activity and Sleep Monitor

text_fidelity_a:
The Flex Belt Abdominal Muscle Toner , Black, 24"-47" Bottom line: If you're looking for a magic solution that will produce firm abs with no effort, keep on looking - this won't do that (nor will anything else!). It is, however, an effective supplement to the usual ab routines. Tha major downside is the price (both initial and on-going).

Full review: Abs are one of the most difficult body parts for me to keep toned since many of the more effective exercises, such as crunches, are difficult for me to do with any degree of intensity due to chronic back problems. This looked like an interesting way to get a low-impact targeting of my abs.

The device is in essence a TENS system. That stands for transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation, and is a technique that has been used for years by physical therapists to help alleviate pain. I was first introduced to TENS therapy when I ruptured a disk and needed a few weeks of physical therapy to help with the recovery process. You can do a search on TENS and get all the specific details but in brief it involves placing pads on your body and applying an electrical charge. I know, that sounds rather Frankenstein-ish, but it's safe (if used properly) and not at all unpleasant.

The belt has three pads that it positions on your abs when you put the belt on. You can adjust the pad position based on your waist size. The manual provides clear instructions as to how/where to place the pads. There are also some very nicely done videos on their website to help with setup and usage.

The unit has a control pad that allows you to select the program and vary the intensity. There are 10 different programs that range from 20 to 40 minutes long. There is a wide range of intensity level adjustments (0 to 150) which vary it from "can't feel it at all" to "please stop!!" I was impressed at the number of settings it offers to control the intensity of the stimulation.

I found the controller to be very easy to use, with a clear display that shows the time and intensity level.

The belt is battery powered. You charge it using the supplied AC adapter. Once charged, you do not need to be plugged into the wall outlet to use it - the battery is built into the device. There's an indicator that tells you when the battery power is low and you need to recharge (which takes a few hours). Battery life is good, with each charge lasting for several sessions.

The belt is comfortable to wear and adjusts easily. I was a bit disappointed in the build quality of the belt, however. Given the price I was expecting something that was more robust. It's OK, but it's not something that wow'ed me in terms of construction quality.

There are ongoing costs in using this in that you have to replace the pads at regular intervals (the manufacturer recommends replacement after 30 uses). The replacement pads are pricy ($15), and you'll want to factor that into the total cost of ownership. You can extend the pad life by using electrode gel (such as this: [[ASIN:B0002CA8RQ Spectra 360 Electrode Gel]]. There are many other brands of gel as well). In addition to keeping the pads usable for a longer time, the gel helps increase conductivity (it's also great to use with heart rate monitors).

So, does it work? Yes - I saw an increase in ab definition after using it. However, it comes with a BIG caveat: the belt alone won't give you perfect abs. You still need to watch your diet and do conventional exercises to keep your weight down so that the flab don't hide the abs. The belt will help fine-tune the process by targeting your abs, but the belt alone won't do squat if you're overweight, or expect it to get you into shape you while you sit on the sofa eating chips.

I'll give it 4 stars since it works well and does what it is supposed to do. The manual is clear, and the product is easy to use. The main downside (and the reason for a loss of one star) is that for the price I was expecting more sturdy-feeling components or have it include more accessories, such as the attachments that you can get to target your arms. At the very least it should include a more ample supply of pads (it comes with one set).

Pricy for what you get, but it does what it says it will do.
[the manufacturer provided the product for review]
text_fidelity_b: The Flex Belt Abdominal Muscle Toner , Black, 24"-47"

Victagen USB Rechargeable Bike Light Sets, Rechargeable Super Bright 2400 Lumens Front Light with Rechargeable Bike Tail Light, Helmet Light, Waterproof Bike Headlamp, Easy Mount Remove and Rotatable Like most low-priced LED lights on amazon, this one overstates its lumen output by quite a bit. Usually they are using LED which are rated up to 2400 lumens but they are not driving them with enough wattage to produce that much light. I have several expensive lights from other manufacturers like Light & Motion and ITUO which I know to be rated accurately. Comparing this light to my ITUO Wiz XP3 (2300 lumens) it is clear that this light is nowhere near as bright. However, comparing to my L&M 1200 lumen light, this one is pretty similar in brightness. The Light & Motion light has a wider beam pattern which is better for cycling.. but this Victagen model performs pretty well and for the price it is an excellent value.

Pros:
Full aluminum enclosure, good for heat dissipation
Weather sealed with Silicon grommets
Rear Battery indicator LEDs
the 2 internal 18650 batteries can be replaced** (see note below)
very bright for the price (true output around 1000-1200 lumens which is plenty bright for most uses)
includes 2 mounts

Cons:
narrow beam pattern, this is somewhat offset by having two LEDs, but it would still be greatly improved by diffusing optics or different reflectors

** Note regarding the 18650 batteries -- you can disassemble this light and replace the internal batteries (they are standard 18650 flat top style); however, it is somewhat easy to break the internal wiring when reassembling if you are not careful, so I would not recommend hot swapping the batteries while on a ride. Even though it is not great for hot-swapping, it is nice to have the option to replace the batteries later if the included ones start to fade quickly, or to replace with higher capacity cells for even more run-time.

text_fidelity_a:
SHIMANO UN55 BB Square Taper Bottom Bracket I only have one ride in with this BB so far, but already I can tell it's a night-and-day improvement over the vintage BB it replaces.

I tooled up to overhaul the old BB on a ca. 1990 Trek, and that went well except for the condition of the spindle; it had already become pitted from foreign objects grinding around in there.

The new UN55 is butter smooth and feels more solid, too.

My only reservation is the spacing. I measured slightly under 113mm on the old spindle, so figured the 113mm UN55 would be the tiniest bit wide. In fact it was a tiny bit narrow, as the chainrings lined up slightly to the left of where they were. I adjusted the limit screw and tension on the front derailleur and the bike seems to work fine now. Not sure whether I should try a wider BB or what; I'm new to proper road bike mechanics. Also I didn't actually measure the new spindle to verify that it really is 113mm; I only noticed the discrepancy after I assembled the whole thing and I didn't want to back out all the parts just to measure....

My UN55 was shipped from Bell's Bike Shop and it was missing the bolts. I had to go to a local store and get a couple of spare bolts from their parts bin.
text_fidelity_b: SHIMANO UN55 BB Square Taper Bottom Bracket

I don't have a lot of money, but I love to fish. One day I decided I was going to treat myself and buy a $150 reel. I spent any hour and a half in Cabela's and about the same at Sportsman's. I tried every reel in the place, and still ended up with the Pres 30. It's just the best feeling reel I've ever used, and I've borrowed plenty over my 40+ years.

But it's not just great to play with in the store. I've caught probably 200 trout on mine, and it's been beat up. Dropped, submerged, dragged through mud, and covered in clay. I treated it the same way I did my Abu ProMax, and that piece of garbage died after 2 months.

If you're looking for a great reel and you have $150 to spend, get this and use the extra money to buy a nice rod, some good copoly line, and gas up your truck. Go fish!

ATEPA Yellow 0 Degree Down Mummy Backpacking Lightweight Sleeping Bag for Women, Girl, Adult, Cold Weather Ultralight Waterproof Compact Sleeping Bag with Compression Sack for Hiking, Camping, Outdoor We have seeking to lighten our backpack load by purchasing lighter items. The grind is many items with quality are so costly. I thought I'd give this bad a try as it lighter than my current bag and rated for a little colder temps. I have yet to use the bag in the field, but it does feel warm and the quality isn't too bad. It's not top of the line, but it's also not 600+ dollars. The zipper is easy to operate, something that even my bag from REI has trouble with. I like the unique zipper shape too. The Zipper works in two directions which is nice since it will go across your legs and up or down your side and over the legs. This will be nice for regulating your body temp as a vent and to allow your feet to hang out if you wish. Heck you could walk with the bag still on if you desired. It has a nice thick baffle to insulate around the zipper and another around your neck and shoulders

We got the regular size bags for weight and cost and we are fine with it, but please note, If you are portly and/or tall, get the long. I'm 5' 7' - 154 pounds and still had several inches length wise and a few width wise, but I could see anyone being over 5' 10' having issues in the regular size bag. It would fit up to 6 ft, but it would be a close fit.

Customer Service was great. The bag itself was in perfect shape, but two of the buckles wouldn't cinch. I contacted them and in very short fashion, they contacted me to make things right. I offered a few suggestions to avoid returning needlessly. They offered a nice refund amount to cover me getting another cinch sack, but I'm just going to get new buckles and sew them on since it won't take long. If you are an outdoor person, you've likely had to replace buckles over the years.

I'm expecting the bag to last for years.

text_fidelity_a:
Nail Drills for Acrylic Nails Professional Electric Nail File, RenoJ Portable Electric Nail Drill Efile Nail Filer Electric (Pink) This is a great little nail drill with lots of positives, but there's still room for improvement. This is basically a miniature Dremel tool for fingernails.

PROS:
• Very quiet.
• USB cord is lighter than electrical cord.
• Nice range of speeds from slow to fast.
• Speeds are variable so you're not stuck with just a few predetermined speeds.
• Can reverse the spin direction.
• Came with more accessories than you'll ever need (and they're in really cute little containers).

NEUTRALS:
• Easy to hold, but still a little bulky. Would be better if it was smaller: thinner and shorter.
• Nice smooth metal case, but it easily slips when holding it – I added a gel pencil grip which stopped the slipping problem.

CONS:
• Must be plugged in to use – it would be great if it had a rechargeable battery.
• Switches for on/off, direction, and speed are inconveniently placed – Instead of being on the tool itself, they're on the cord, about a foot away from the tool. You have to reach down the cord for each adjustment. They move around as the cord moves.
• The drill rolls – Anytime you put it down, it rolls away. The cord can help limit the rolling, but when it's unplugged, there is nothing to stop it from rolling off the table. I put a gel pencil grip on the drill to help stop this.
• The nail bits are kept in two mismatched plastic containers with different lengths, widths, and thicknesses. When combined with the bag for the sanding bands, you end up needing a container to hold all the containers! It would be better if at least the nail bits were all in one, single container.

Overall, this is a good little tool for filing nails. Hopefully, newer versions will be even better.
text_fidelity_b: Nail Drills for Acrylic Nails Professional Electric Nail File, RenoJ Portable Electric Nail Drill Efile Nail Filer Electric (Pink)
